newsitem.title: FRANCE: Wheat bids put EU in reach of 1 mln T sales so far.
newsitem.headline: Wheat bids put EU in reach of 1 mln T sales so far.

text.p: A flurry of French bids for European Union wheat export licences, if accepted, would push the amount of EU soft wheat grain committed so far this season to just over one million tonnes, EU figures show.
They would also bring the full volume of soft wheat awards including those for flour to slightly over 2.2 million tonnes.

French cereals office ONIC said on Monday it had received bids on Friday for 722,500 tonnes of soft wheat export through the EU's daily bidding channel, which currently has an export tax of 0.50 Ecus a tonne.
The European Commission, which has not said what volume it would find acceptable for now, has until mid-week to decide whether to exercise its three-day veto over the bids.
The volume of bidding has soared as European prices move closer to, and in some cases overlap with, U.S. values partly because of the surge in the value of the dollar.

On July 31 the EU awarded 170,000 tonnes of soft wheat for export at a minimum tax of 0.50 Ecus per tonne at its routine export tender. Commission figures show it had previously awarded 162,000 tonnes since the season began on July 1.
Total export awards for soft wheat up to July 29 were 1.319 million tonnes. That included 1.148 million tonnes of soft wheat flour when expressed in grain equivalent terms.
The EU crop marketing season runs from July to June.
